If you prefer the term "cornercase", then I'll use it. Remember the precise
card text : "Master: out-of-turn. Put this card on a Giovanni when you move
that Giovanni from your uncontrolled region to your ready region during your
influence phase. This Giovanni gains one level of Potence [pot] and one
level of Fortitude [for]. His or her capacity is increased by 1. Move 1
blood from the blood bank to this Giovanni."

This means that :

1) It concerns solely strategies based on Pot / For, and / or strategies
that involve Giovanni growing in capacity

2) The time-window is pathetically short : when the Giovanni comes into
control during the Influence phase. Meaning that if you have them in hand
after you control your "main minions", you'll have to either discard them or
keep them in hand until you get a chance to get another one out (usually
after your first kill. In other words, either you put lots in your deck and
it will cluster it, or you don't put too many and it will probably be
useless. I'll grant you that Legendary Vampire uses a similar window, but
the impact on the game is quite different and justifies putting several in
your deck to get it early.

3) Of course it concerns only Giovanni : if you make a mixed crypt this will
benefit very few of your guys, and even fewer who don't already have POT
(and therefore would just need a For skill) if you rely on guys like
Ignazio, Benedict, Baldesar...

So, all in all, I will very seldom play such a card, while the Tumninos,
Waters of Duat and Web of Knives give a real edge to the concerned clans.

> And given past results (such as winning a storyline event and being
> towards the top of others, plus many constructed tournament wins), do
> the Giovanni really "NEED" yet another (boring, overused) way to win
> games?

that's why they were given those too. Giovanni have Dom ? Sure, so what :
Setites can bleed you down too, Ravnos have Week of Nightmares... Only the

Well, no more than playing only what they already can. Wasn't the Ravnos
Embrace deck already boring ? Still, they made Tumninos, with some
restrictions but some advantages. It is rather less boring than before,
having 1 new option...

> Seems to me they do pretty well without it, and thus I'd much
> rather see new, creative tools for them rather than a slightly-
> customized spawn 'like the other indies got'.

I'll be very happy to see them get new tools too. But I'd like to see this

But, see, combat doesn't actually do anything to them. Unless you have a
million minions to hospitalize them *and* pillowface them in the same
turn. And if you have a lot of minions, they are probably small. So they
get Convictioned into torpor after the pillowfacing.

Beating up an Imbued is easy, except that you can't Haven Uncovered
them, Fame them, or Taste their Vitae (or Disarm or Decapitate them...),
all of which are a drag for a combat deck. And when you do beat them
into the hospital, they are coming out of the hospital at the start of
the next turn, regardless of whose turn it is for 2 conviction with no
action at all due to Jennie (as every Imbued deck uses Jennie). So
beating them into the hospital isn't doing much other than letting you
spin your wheels.

Yeah, you can probably kill and eat every Imbued that hits the table if
you are playing a dedicated Rush deck before they take any actions and
get set up at all, in which case you are just giving your grand prey a
totally free ride while you whittle away the Imbued pool sack. Which
isn't horrible if you are the Imbued's predator, but if you are the Rush
deck and the Imbued is *your* predator? You are just going to spend the
whole game backousting and give the game to your prey?

> i think that their success in tournaments derives much from the fact,
> that tournament players (from a reason unknown to me) tend to be all
> waiting, "table balance", "table talk" and such bullshit, which is an

I'm amazed at the statement that if you don't let them tool up they
are easy. That applies to many decks, not just imbued. However, not
all imbued decks need to tool up. And I don't know 'bout you. But how
many non potence or animalism decks can deal with a conceal Flash
Grenade, which is my weapon of choice with them. I don't actually like
playing them, but I built the deck because I got enough cards from the
Prerelease to build one. And to show how dangerous they could be. Not
because I actually bought any more. Which I didn't, but that's another
point.

A few clans have little trouble killing Imbued. Assamites for example
have a couple cards that do extra damage to allies. Their Contracts
allow them to rush them. Potence clans should have no problems dunking
them. Tzimisce as well. However, Gehenna is more problematic than some
mentioned. I had one game where I had so many Gehenna out, that all
the Vamps were lower in capacity than me, there was no cam or sabbat,
and disciplines were hard to play.

I wouldn't expect an Assamite Seraph. Unless they made one and then
had an ADV version where he went Indy. Which is what happened with at
least one of the former Seraphs in the RPG. Also, quietus is quite
alright. Aside from a bounce or bleed fails card, a proactive counter
to SCE for Assamites, and a Succubus Club in order to extort pool from
"marks." That's what the Assamites need.

Setites need a cool affordable Bane Mummy along the lines of Ambrosius
or the Hordes. Where the snakes will build a deck using him or her. As
well as some alternate means of combat.

Ravnos desperately need an ADV vamp. And they need some new tricks up
their sleeves.

Giovanni, need some new useful Necro tricks and allies. I'd also like
to see at least one or two more Gio with Pot\Fort in some capacity.

If you aren't a dedicated Rush deck, you aren't going to kill them
effectively if they are your prey. If you demonstrate that you can
reliably block them with +2 intercept early on, they just stop powering
up and go forward instead. If you are their prey, walling up to stop the
Imbued isn't getting you far, in the forward momentum direction.

> the other thread about weenie POT, as mentioned above.

Yeah, see, the weenie POT decks that actually win games *don't* spend
the whole game backousting. 'Cause then they just, maybe, get 2VPs.
Which does not a game win make. And you can get 2VPs by being the last
deck standing with a million different, all mostly bad, decks.

> but seriously. they CAN be really strong, IF you give them time to set
> up. that's what I'm saying. read more, write less :)

*If* you give them time to set up. Sometimes you have no choice.
Sometimes, it is a bad idea to just vaporize them from the get go, as
they are your predator. See, you seem to be under the impression that it
is somehow good for the game to act irrationally in the face of the
Imbued (i.e. switch into "must kill them regardless of where they are at
the table!" mode when you see them, rather than "play a sane game of
VTES" mode), which it is not. If you just back oust them, all you do is
make someone else win the game. If you just cross table destroy them,
you just make someone else win the game.

As I said in my reply to Peter, I'm partly joking here. I play against
a LOT of animalism here in Atlanta. And it beats me a fair amount of
the time, though a lot of that has to do with the fact that I'm
playing against good players who've adapted well to the existence of
the imbued (and the fact that I play them so much).

Still, animalism has a lot to recommend itself against the imbued:

1) Permacept (stops power build-up)
2) Crows + Bats (gets around Memories of Mortality, avoids simple
Strike With Conviction combat)
3) Untap (negates Flash-Grenade lockdown)
4) Canine Horde/Terror Frenzy (stops other equipment-based imbued
strategies, including shutting down Cleave pretty hard)

And all of these things are going to be in your deck _anyway_. There's
nothing specifically anti-imbued about it, except maybe that you're
using Terror Frenzy (which works on imbued) instead of Drawing Out the
Beast (which doesn't).

> The ways I've seen Imbued get killed are:
>
> 1) stealth vote
> 2) the Imbued deck sucks or is played badly
> 3) massive stealth bleed
> 4) Smiling Jack that didn't get Suddened or contested by the Imbued deck

That's mostly it, though there's more to the game than not-dying.

Last game I played it was point 4 that killed me directly, but there
was no way I was going to oust my ANI prey anyway. She had way too
much untap and enough intercept (i.e., 1) to counter any Second Sight
on forward actions. I'd get a couple bleeds through, but not enough to
stop her from ousting her prey. Add Anarch Revolt here (three of these
ousted me one game in the NAC - though only because the other two
players left in the game ganged up on me).

Point 3 is the only reason I still include Champion in decks (and the
only reason Paralyze This! has any powers in it at all). It's a
craptacularly bad card in 90% of the games I play, but I still feel
like I have to hamper myself with it because somebody might bleed me
for 9 at 7 stealth.

Add in to point 2 the possibility that the imbued just gets deck-
screwed. I've had it happen to me enough times (with decks that are
normally very reliable) to know that it can hurt. Especially if the
other players pick up on it and act accordingly.

And Stealth-Vote sucks a lot, too.

Witness1

> Overall, the art has been quite good in the past few sets,
> with few exceptions. Though I think my favorite set ever artwise is
> still LoB. Especially the Osebo crypt looks awesome.

you mean the osebo ?
-Cesewao (abrar ajmal) is good, yes. Dynamic and impressive.

-Homa (ken meyer jr) is plain crap.

-Idrissa (matt mitchell) is just too awful and awkward to pass as a 3
years old kid's creation. Really, it's a piece of cat poo : if you don't
believe me look at the picture hosted by vtes.pl
http://vtes.pl/index.php?m=2&szukv=848&ln=en (by the way, i've always
wanted thank you for the database, guys ! ;) )

-Ismitta (rebecca guay) is ok as a portrait but in no way looks like a
vampire. At most, it's a student or teacher. Not a bloodsucking monster.

-Kamaria (rebecca guay) Good, but hey, we want vampires, not a mage from
magic the gathering. Or does auspex and potence allow you to create
miraculous globes of lights ? In any case the illustration is by no mean
what you could expect from an african vampire.

-Khalu (ken meyer jr) Despite the awkward anatomic depiction of this
character, i must say the illustration tries to convey something. It's a
nice illustration which serves its purpose right, imho.

-Massassi (Arbar ajmal) the thematic is good, the character looks scary
and has a good attitude. not to mention big breasts. I'm ok with this
one (even with the cheesy see-through tunic ;) )

-Misrak (rebecca guay) is jacky brown in a green dress. Looks african
enough, with the stick (all african carry sticks when they walk around,
you didn't know ? ) and regarding her capacity, looks quite like a
human. So I am ok with this one.

-Tatu Sawosa (ken meyer jr) has some skeletal problems... Or is it the
leopard coming out of her ass ?? :) The picture is cheesy AND badly
executed. Look at the legs for caine's sake ! And the same cheesy
background of cloudy sky and vaguely savanna looking vegetation
copyrighted by ken meyer jr. C.R.A.P. Come on Ken, i know what you did
in the previous sets... You painted some very good art (succubus,
Lisette Vizquel). What happened to you ?

-Uzoma (Rik Martin) is a fighter, has scraification, is scary. I'm not
fond of Rik's art, but at least it is representative of the game.
Despite the lacking of a proper background i'll say that I like it.

-Kisha bilji (Ken meyer jr) is interesting. Cheesy and malformed lion
put aside, it's quite good. the character looks wise, which incidentally
goes along with the title. The fact she is represented by day is ok
since laibon have aye and stuff to help them endure the sunlight iirc.
At least it is in the mood of the LOB expansion. I'd say i like it
despite the background of cloudy sky and all...

With half ov the vampires being crap, i must say it's not the clan who
got the best treatment from LoB.
Again, i'm only a player and not an art teacher, i have only an
'awesome' view on this :)

r.

Heart of Nizchetus

> Pot\Fort\Nec\Dom just not have all kinds of appeal. Grapple, Dead
> Hand, Disarm, Decap. Prevent as needed.

Sure. Proxy Kissed is a real good card if you can actually play it.
But the huge honking problem with it is that the opportunity to play it is so
limited. It's like Legendary Vampire except you have to be holding it
during your influence phase (a slight disadvantage, I think, as you couldn't
draw into it over the course of other players' turns). And it's not nearly as
a good a card as Legendary Vampire, which repays its opportunity cost downside
much more handsomely. I just don't think Proxy Kissed is worth bothering
with unless you can think of a deck where your vampires are going in and out
of the uncontrolled area constantly or something.

Fred
